Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Apple’s Business Approach & Next steps

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.
*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.
    ◦ Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.
*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*
If you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:
1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*
    ◦ AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).
    ◦ You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.
2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*
    ◦ Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don’t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.
    ◦ Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.
3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*
    ◦ Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).
*Bottom Line*
Your current idea *will likely violate policies* and could get you *banned from major ad networks*. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

input.prompt:
You have Slack MCP tools (mcp__hg__slack_*) and Linear tools (mcp__hg__linear_*). Read-only research; do not post or modify anything.

1. Read the ENTIRE Slack channel #bridge-pitch (channel id C096HFA5Z8W) from Aug 25, 2025 through Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC, including all thread replies (use slack_read_channel with oldest=1756080000 and paginate via cursor; for every message with reply_count, read the thread with slack_read_thread). Report every message nearly verbatim with timestamp (UTC and Pacific), author, and text. Pay attention to: investors/firms/angels pitched, calls/meetings, who passed or declined (and whether they told us directly or via Griffin/an advisor), intros made by IH, Matthew, or advisors, SAFE/signing, amounts.

2. Find everything about internal build tester access for investors: TestFlight (iOS) and Google Play internal test track (Android) tester adds — who (which investor firm / which people) were added, removed, invites failed, or couldn't access. Arthur Blake tracks the tester adds. Search Slack across all channels and DMs (slack_conversations_search_messages / slack_search_public_and_private) for terms like TestFlight, tester, "internal test", "Play internal", "Play Console", invite, build access, and read relevant threads. Also search Linear issues (linear_list_issues with query like TestFlight, tester, investor build) and read any matching issue and its comments. Report all findings with dates and authors, nearly verbatim.

make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
The user wants read-only research. The instruction is verbatim: "Read-only research; do not post or modify anything." The deliverable is a long, detailed plain-text report with no files written. It has three parts:
   (1) Read all of #bridge-pitch (C096HFA5Z8W) from Aug 25, 2025 to Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC. Use slack_read_channel with oldest=1756080000, page through with the cursor, and read every thread that has replies with slack_read_thread. Report each message nearly verbatim with its timestamp in UTC and Pacific, its author and its text. Focus on:
   - investors pitched
   - calls and meetings
   - passes and declines, and whether we heard directly or through Griffin or an advisor
   - intros made by IH, Matthew or advisors
   - SAFE and signing
   - amounts
   (2) Find all tester access given to investors for internal builds: TestFlight on iOS and the Google Play internal test track on Android. Cover who was added or removed, which invites failed, and who couldn't get access. Arthur Blake tracks these adds. Search all Slack channels and DMs for TestFlight, tester, "internal test", "Play internal", "Play Console", invite and build access. Also search Linear issues for TestFlight, tester and investor build, including comments. Report with dates and authors.
   (3) Search Slack for Aug 25 – Oct 1, 2025 mentions of these firms and people:
   - LVP/London Venture Partners, Play Ventures, Transcend, Initial Capital, Makers Fund, March Gaming, a16z/speedrun
   - Dentsu, Hiro, Grishin, Raine, General Catalyst, Gorkem/Görkem, Lakestar, BBQ Capital, T-accelerate
   - NCsoft, Mattel, SciPlay, Superplay, Sony, Revo, e2vc, Acterra, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem, GFR Fund, Brightwater
   - Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri, Anton Bernstein, Paul Heydon, Griffin, Edith Vane, Rohan Jain

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Slack MCP tools:
     - slack_read_channel (newest first, cursor paging; latest=1759302000 is Oct 1 07:00 UTC)
     - slack_read_thread
     - slack_search_public_and_private and slack_conversations_search_messages
   - Linear tools: linear_list_issues, linear_get_issue, linear_list_comments
   - Pacific time in this period is PDT, i.e. UTC-7.
   - Likely author identities:
     - EMPLOYEE_0038: Leonard Hayes, CEO (leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co)
     - EMPLOYEE_0016: co-founder with the Applovin contact
     - EMPLOYEE_0025: build engineer, probably Arthur Blake, who adds testers
   - Company and games: Harmony Games, formerly Calm Play LLC; games are Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D. Backed by Griffin Gaming Partners.

3. Files and Code Sections: None. No files were read or written.

4. Errors and fixes: None.

5. Problem Solving / Findings so far:

#bridge-pitch page 1 (newest first; UTC timestamps, PDT = UTC-7)

Sep 28, 2025 ~18:50 UTC (11:50 PDT), all EMPLOYEE_0038:
- ts 1759085462: "I started to see people announcing their acceptance to speedrun from [USERNAME_1453] and the application deadline is closing 2 days"
- ts 1759085484: "I don't think it's happening for us. We will likely get a rejection letter later this week or next"
- ts 1759085532: "I also noticed my friend [PERSON_NAME_25249] announcing his plan at ncsoft on LinkedIn"
- ts 1759085550: a LinkedIn link (taewonyun post)

Sep 26:
- ts 1758927000, 22:50 UTC (15:50 PDT), 0038: "told Mattel we're passing on the Barbie RFP. since the kickoff that's only been an RFP conversation, we haven't pitched them the bridge"

Sep 25 ~19:46 UTC, 0038:
- ts 1758829538: "pinged [USERNAME_0458] just now"
- ts 1758829572: "I'm trying to schedule time with tapnation but their game acquisition guys' meeting slots are 2am-6:30am my local time"
- ts 1758829580: "trying to see if the has some flexibility"
- ts 1758829656: booked an earlier one-way flight to LA (Alaska saver fare); "Worst case this meeting is gonna cost us an extra $250"
- ts 1758829663: "not a big deal in grand scheme of things"

Sep 25, other:
- ts 1758822451, 0016: "Well, gaming is hard, the biz model is figured out, but getting on the right path with the right game is hard…"
- ts 1758817200, 16:20 UTC (09:20 PDT), 0038: "correction on Play Ventures: the no I pasted here on the 15th was what they told Griffin, not us. that's why I said they never answered us. it's still their no for this round, the "discussing" Robert heard via Applovin doesn't change that"
- ts 1758811165, ~14:39 UTC, 0038: "I'm sure you guys have seen it but sharing the rejection note from [PERSON_NAME_7818]". The full email followed. Key points:
  - It opens "Hey Leonard, Really sorry for the delayed reply, we were away last week in Istanbul…"
  - "unfortunately, we won't be joining this round"
  - They cite "content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP"
  - "later-stage financing for mobile teams right now seems largely concentrated on studios in Turkey"
  - Signed [PERSON_NAME_29501]
  - The Istanbul trip suggests a Turkey-linked firm.
- ts 1758811177, 0038: "I think in their case they want to fund us but not for this lol"

Sep 25 ~04:00 UTC (Sep 24 ~21:00 PDT):
- 0038: "yeah, anything that can help us float the company"
- 0038: "the challenge is co-devs usually take much longer to close"

Sep 25 ~03:30 UTC:
- 0016: "I would love a co-dev deal probably more than funding"
- 0016: "But beggars can't be choosers"

Sep 25 ~02:30 UTC (Sep 24 ~19:30 PDT):
- 0016: "[PERSON_NAME_8105] from Applovin said [PERSON_NAME_37299] is aware that you reached out" / (blank) / "Play Ventures"
- 0038: "LOL. They did not even acknowledge us" / "But thank you" / "And say thx to [PERSON_NAME_8105]"
- 0016: "\"discussing\""
- 0038: "Discussing usually involves a party of 2" / "At least they should let us know they are not moving forward as a courtesy"
- 0038, ts 1758767624: "In either case I'm not really feeling too excited nowadays about our chance of raising… At this point in time I give us a 15% chance to raise funding."
- 0038: "I didn't give up but I'm also prepping for the more likely outcome…"
- 0038: "Either someone is gonna fall in love with zombie match or someone will bite into our engine vision" / "I don't see either happening yet"

     import json,base64,sys,re,html
     def dec(s): return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(s+'='*(-len(s)%4)).decode('utf-8','replace')
     def walk(p,out):

             pl=[x for x in out if x[0]=='text/plain']

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
The user wants read-only research. The constraint, verbatim: "Read-only research; do not post or modify anything." The deliverable is a long, detailed plain-text report with no files written. It has three parts.

Part 1: Read all of #bridge-pitch (C096HFA5Z8W) from Aug 25, 2025 to Oct 1, 2025 07:00 UTC.
- Use slack_read_channel with oldest=1756080000, page through with the cursor, and read every thread that has replies.
- Report each message nearly verbatim with UTC and Pacific timestamps, author and text.
- Focus on:
  - investors pitched
  - calls and meetings
  - passes, and whether they came directly or via Griffin or an advisor
  - intros by IH, Matthew or advisors
  - SAFE and signing
  - amounts

Part 2: Find all investor tester access to internal builds (TestFlight on iOS, the Play internal test track on Android).
- Cover who was added or removed, failed invites, and who couldn't get access. Arthur Blake tracks these.
- Search all Slack for TestFlight, tester, "internal test", "Play internal", "Play Console", invite and build access.
- Search Linear issues and comments for TestFlight, tester and investor build.
- Report with dates and authors.

Part 3: Search Slack from Aug 25 to Oct 1, 2025 for these firms and people:
- LVP/London Venture Partners, Play Ventures, Transcend, Initial Capital, Makers Fund, March Gaming, a16z/speedrun
- Dentsu, Hiro, Grishin, Raine, General Catalyst, Gorkem/Görkem, Lakestar, BBQ Capital, T-accelerate
- NCsoft, Mattel, SciPlay, Superplay, Sony, Revo, e2vc, Acterra, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem, GFR Fund, Brightwater
- Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri, Anton Bernstein, Paul Heydon, Griffin, Edith Vane, Rohan Jain

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- Slack MCP tools:
  - slack_read_channel: returns newest first; latest=1759302000; concise format shows thread_ts but not reply_count
  - slack_read_thread
  - slack_search_public_and_private
- Linear tools: linear_list_issues, linear_get_issue, linear_list_comments
- PDT = UTC-7.
- Author identities:
  - EMPLOYEE_0038: Leonard Hayes, CEO
  - EMPLOYEE_0016: co-founder with the Applovin contact
  - EMPLOYEE_0025: likely Arthur Blake, the build engineer who adds testers
  - EMPLOYEE_0008: senior team member or advisor (school-run dad) who gave Homa strategy feedback
- Company: Harmony Games, formerly Calm Play LLC. Backed by Griffin Gaming Partners ($3M seed). Games are Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.
- Four background Gmail-reading agents (batches A–D) are running. Do not duplicate them. Their output files are at /tmp/claude-0/-app/064531c9-147a-4221-bd47-3e6e25d14258/tasks/<id>.output.

3. Files and Code Sections: None. No files were read or written.

4. Errors and fixes: None.

5. Problem Solving / Findings so far:

#bridge-pitch page 1 (Sep 23–28), from the earlier summary

Sep 28 ~18:50 UTC / 11:50 PDT, 0038:
- Speedrun acceptances are being announced; "I don't think it's happening for us. We will likely get a rejection letter later this week or next."
- A friend announced a plan at NCsoft (LinkedIn link).

Sep 26 22:50 UTC (ts 1758927000), 0038:
- "told Mattel we're passing on the Barbie RFP. since the kickoff that's only been an RFP conversation, we haven't pitched them the bridge"

Sep 25 ~19:46 UTC, 0038:
- Pinged [USERNAME_0458].
- TapNation game-acquisition meeting slots are 2am–6:30am local time.
- Booked an earlier flight to LA; "Worst case this meeting is gonna cost us an extra $250."

Sep 25 16:20 UTC (ts 1758817200), 0038:
- "correction on Play Ventures: the no I pasted here on the 15th was what they told Griffin, not us. that's why I said they never answered us. it's still their no for this round, the "discussing" Robert heard via Applovin doesn't change that"

Sep 25 ~14:39 UTC (ts 1758811165), 0038 shared a rejection email from [PERSON_NAME_7818]:
- "away last week in Istanbul"
- "we won't be joining this round"
- "content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP"
- "later-stage financing for mobile teams right now seems largely concentrated on studios in Turkey"
- Signed [PERSON_NAME_29501].
- 0038 followed with: "I think in their case they want to fund us but not for this lol"

Sep 25 ~02:30–04:00 UTC:
- 0016: [PERSON_NAME_8105] from Applovin says Play Ventures is "discussing" Harmony.
- 0038: "They did not even acknowledge us."
- 0038 (ts 1758767624): "I give us a 15% chance to raise funding."
- On co-dev: 0016 said he would prefer a co-dev deal over funding; 0038 said "co-devs usually take much longer to close."

Sep 24 ~00:00–01:30 UTC (Sep 23 PDT), Dentsu:
- 0038 (ts 1758672395): "we are meeting with Dentsu in 25 mins."
- 0016 noted Dentsu is a Japanese conglomerate with a marketing agency arm.
- After the meeting: "impossible to read what they think."
- 0038 planned to send a follow-up offering the Google Play link and asked 0025 whether it would work.
- 0038: "we are also talking to [USERNAME_37108] tomorrow morning."
- 0025 (ts 1758677722): "I have to add them by email for google play to work."
- 0038: "ok, I'll ask for their emails then," then "done" (ts 1758678763).

Sep 23 ~23:30 UTC, Play Ventures discussion:
- 0016 (ts 1758671427): Play Ventures didn't respond; [PERSON_NAME_8105] offered to reach out.
- 0038:
  - "they don't invest in mobile content"
  - "I emailed them back on Sept 3rd"
  - (ts 1758671857) "[USERNAME_32018], Matthew or [PERSON_NAME_6550] didn't ping them either"
  - "we really didn't get much help from our advisors when it came to the pitches this time around"

Hi PERSON_0558_NAME and the team,

I hope all has been well since we last touched base. We appreciated the
support and understood that LVP was uncomfortable with mobile back in 2023.
I wanted to reconnect and see if There has been any shift in your thesis
and whether you might consider participating in our upcoming round.

We are kicking off a $2.5M bridge this week to advance our AI-driven
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and beta launch our innovative Match & Slash puzzle RPG. Why
this investment could be quite attractive:

AI-native studio: Engine built with AI at the core of design, content

Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
An innovative puzzle RPG on mobile: Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for
Western audiences with day-one liveops.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn with ~$100K/month
opex, rapid iteration and multiple shots at goal.

If this fits your current investment thesis, we would be delighted to grab
30–45 minutes this week or the next 2 weeks.

===  Fri, 12 Sep 2025 17:24:19 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thanks again for the time and the sharp questions earlier this week - we
found the discussion genuinely useful. We were a bit underprepared to
summarize our takeaways from Domino Delights on the call, so I’m sending a
clearer follow-up below and highlighting a few points that I wanted to get
across.

*Why we’re excited about LVP*
We know this market is hard. We’re looking for a lead who believes an
*engine-first &
multiple-shots at goal approach* can unlock scale; we simply didn’t raise
enough last time to fully lean into it. We also know you guys are awesome
and can really support us in our journey beyond capital injection.

*Try the current build*
We pushed an update yesterday (levels *100 → 200* plus major technical
fixes) and are gearing up for *beta-2 build*. We have 3 major features and
some polish shipping next Friday and will follow up with hopefully some
exciting KPIs, especially around playtime.

   -

   iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
   -

   Android:
   https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US

*Partnerships & roadmap*
We’re leaning into publisher/partnerships to expand capability. Next week
we have an engine deep-dive with a potential partner and will draft a
3-year engine roadmap - what [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine looks like with 10+ engineers,
Unity plugins/SDK, and a platform that operates as a growth machine. We’ll
share those notes with you to inform your process.

*Domino Delights Learnings*

*Don'ts*

   -

   Ship innovations that conflict with the game’s natural audience or theme.
   -

   Over-commit to features with unproven incremental value (e.g., saga map,
   heavy hero animations).
   -

   Build without a strong core-game engagement loop. (This is key and why
   we moved on to Zombie Match 3D)
   -

   Over-iterate on supporting mechanics (mini-games) at the expense of the
   core. - we lost too much time for unproven mini-games and mini-games act
   more like a multiplier to engagement rather than additive so don't do
   mini-games before core is Proven
   -

   Create mismatches between hero progression design and scoring mechanics.
   -

   Interrupt new players with long, text-heavy tutorials.

*Do's*

   -

   Invest in the tile/level engine; create puzzles algorithmically to scale
   core co[USERNAME_6805].
   -

   Build *reusable* LiveOps features and tools that complement the core
   game.
   -

   Stick with Proven core mechanics; apply small, audience-aware tweaks -
   especially for change-resistant segments.
   -

   Choose an art style aligned with the target audience’s preferences.
   -

   Introduce new mechanics gradually if the audience is change-resistant.
   -

   Communicate core mechanics visually and clearly.

Thanks again, and we’d love to continue the conversation if There is
interest. We’re hungry to prove this - chips on our shoulders, and the
experience to first survive, then thrive.

Best,
Leonard

[quoted...]

===  Thu, 25 Sep 2025 15:13:29 +0100 | From: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hey Leonard,

Really sorry for the delayed reply, we were away last week in Istanbul and
it was tough to find time to sync internally. Thanks again for walking me
through the updates with [SOURCE_ORG_0001], I really enjoyed the conversation! I
managed to catch up with the rest of the investment team and unfortunately,
we won’t be joining this round.

That said, I want to say how much we respect what you’re building. The
speed at which you’ve been able to stand up the [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and move
from Domino Delights to Zombie Match 3D is i[USERNAME_6804], and it’s clear the
team has the right mix of experience and execution chops. Ultimately,
though, we don’t feel [SOURCE_ORG_0001] is the right fit for us at this stage. The
content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP in the current
environment feels higher than we’re comfortable with. In addition,
later-stage financing for mobile teams right now seems largely concentrated
on studios in Turkey, which makes it harder for teams outside that cluster
to attract the follow-on capital required to scale UA.

We get this stuff wrong all the time but wanted to be candid about where we
fell short in case it is helpful for the others conversations that you are
having. We are wishing you all the best and will be cheering you on from
the sidelines!

Best,

PERSON_2574_NAME

[quoted...]

===  Fri, 26 Sep 2025 15:16:23 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thank you for the thoughtful note and the kind words. We completely
understand your perspective, and the sentiment around content and market
risk in puzzle IP right now is fair. When we reach the right growth phase,
we plan to expand the studio footprint to Turkey to take advantage of the
deep talent pool and government subsidies we qualify for (since we have a
[NATIONALITY_0151] co-founder), but the timing isn’t There yet.

I’m not worried about scaling UA when the product has the metrics, but I
agree that in today’s environment, distribution challenges add risk. If our
trajectory meaningfully changes and we reduce those challenges, I’ll be
sure to keep you in the loop.

Still, we really value the conversation, your vote of confidence means a
lot, and we look forward to finding a way to work together in the future.

Best,
Leonard

===  Fri, 12 Sep 2025 17:24:19 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thanks again for the time and the sharp questions earlier this week - we
found the discussion genuinely useful. We were a bit underprepared to
summarize our takeaways from Domino Delights on the call, so I’m sending a
clearer follow-up below and highlighting a few points that I wanted to get
across.

*Why we’re excited about LVP*
We know this market is hard. We’re looking for a lead who believes an
*engine-first &
multiple-shots at goal approach* can unlock scale; we simply didn’t raise
enough last time to fully lean into it. We also know you guys are awesome
and can really support us in our journey beyond capital injection.

*Try the current build*
We pushed an update yesterday (levels *100 → 200* plus major technical
fixes) and are gearing up for *beta-2 build*. We have 3 major features and
some polish shipping next Friday and will follow up with hopefully some
exciting KPIs, especially around playtime.

   -

   iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
   -

   Android:
   https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US

*Partnerships & roadmap*
We’re leaning into publisher/partnerships to expand capability. Next week
we have an engine deep-dive with a potential partner and will draft a
3-year engine roadmap - what [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine looks like with 10+ engineers,
Unity plugins/SDK, and a platform that operates as a growth machine. We’ll
share those notes with you to inform your process.

*Domino Delights Learnings*

*Don'ts*

   -

   Ship innovations that conflict with the game’s natural audience or theme.
   -

   Over-commit to features with unproven incremental value (e.g., saga map,
   heavy hero animations).
   -

   Build without a strong core-game engagement loop. (This is key and why
   we moved on to Zombie Match 3D)
   -

   Over-iterate on supporting mechanics (mini-games) at the expense of the
   core. - we lost too much time for unproven mini-games and mini-games act
   more like a multiplier to engagement rather than additive so don't do
   mini-games before core is Proven
   -

   Create mismatches between hero progression design and scoring mechanics.
   -

   Interrupt new players with long, text-heavy tutorials.

*Do's*

   -

   Invest in the tile/level engine; create puzzles algorithmically to scale
   core co[USERNAME_6805].
   -

   Build *reusable* LiveOps features and tools that complement the core
   game.
   -

   Stick with Proven core mechanics; apply small, audience-aware tweaks -
   especially for change-resistant segments.
   -

   Choose an art style aligned with the target audience’s preferences.
   -

   Introduce new mechanics gradually if the audience is change-resistant.
   -

   Communicate core mechanics visually and clearly.

Thanks again, and we’d love to continue the conversation if There is
interest. We’re hungry to prove this - chips on our shoulders, and the
experience to first survive, then thrive.

Best,
Leonard

[quoted...]

===  Thu, 25 Sep 2025 15:13:29 +0100 | From: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hey Leonard,

Really sorry for the delayed reply, we were away last week in Istanbul and
it was tough to find time to sync internally. Thanks again for walking me
through the updates with [SOURCE_ORG_0001], I really enjoyed the conversation! I
managed to catch up with the rest of the investment team and unfortunately,
we won’t be joining this round.

That said, I want to say how much we respect what you’re building. The
speed at which you’ve been able to stand up the [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine and move
from Domino Delights to Zombie Match 3D is i[USERNAME_6804], and it’s clear the
team has the right mix of experience and execution chops. Ultimately,
though, we don’t feel [SOURCE_ORG_0001] is the right fit for us at this stage. The
content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP in the current
environment feels higher than we’re comfortable with. In addition,
later-stage financing for mobile teams right now seems largely concentrated
on studios in Turkey, which makes it harder for teams outside that cluster
to attract the follow-on capital required to scale UA.

We get this stuff wrong all the time but wanted to be candid about where we
fell short in case it is helpful for the others conversations that you are
having. We are wishing you all the best and will be cheering you on from
the sidelines!

Best,

PERSON_2574_NAME

[quoted...]

===  Fri, 26 Sep 2025 15:16:23 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_2574_NAME <PERSON_2574_EMAIL> | Cc: PERSON_0558_NAME <PERSON_0558_EMAIL>, robert@harmonygames.co, arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, PERSON_3663_NAME <PERSON_3663_EMAIL>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: re-intros: Are (LVP) <> Leonard & [PERSON_NAME_0054] ([SOURCE_ORG_0001])
Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thank you for the thoughtful note and the kind words. We completely
understand your perspective, and the sentiment around content and market
risk in puzzle IP right now is fair. When we reach the right growth phase,
we plan to expand the studio footprint to Turkey to take advantage of the
deep talent pool and government subsidies we qualify for (since we have a
[NATIONALITY_0151] co-founder), but the timing isn’t There yet.

I’m not worried about scaling UA when the product has the metrics, but I
agree that in today’s environment, distribution challenges add risk. If our
trajectory meaningfully changes and we reduce those challenges, I’ll be
sure to keep you in the loop.

Still, we really value the conversation, your vote of confidence means a
lot, and we look forward to finding a way to work together in the future.

Best,
Leonard

[quoted...]

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,
It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:
   1.
   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.
   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.
   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:
   [URL_11306]
Looking forward to hearing from you next week.
Best regards,
Leonard

Hi Leonard and [PERSON_NAME_0036],
Thank you for taking the time to explore Balancy today! This is the *demo
free to share with your design and product teams!
Here’s what’s new:
   -
   *Visual LiveOps Calendar*
   Create, drag, reschedule, and organize events with full calendar control.
   -
   *UI Builder*
   Build and customize in-game offers, passes, and messages with zero
   coding - fully visual and templated.
   -
   *Pre-made templates*
   Use ready-made events from top games like *Royal Match*, then adapt them
   to your needs.
   -
   *Engine-agnostic SDK*
   Works beyond Unity - including engines like Cocos or custom clients.
Below is the summary of the features we explored. Our platform can help
your team in several key areas:
*1. LiveOps Events Management*
Introduce time-limited and seasonal activities to keep players engaged and
returning for more.
[image: image.png]
*2. A/B testing.*
Test and optimize any game element — from level difficulty to offer pricing

input.body:
Leonard,

Done. The send list is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (Google Sheet, you have edit access). It covers everyone from the bridge round as of end of day Tue Sep 30 PT, grouped per your doc.

Counts per group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25,000. DocuSign Completed Sep 26 on the re-sent $25K SAFE)
- In talks: 8 firms, 0 angels (a16z, NCsoft, Dentsu Ventures, SciPlay, T-Accelerate, GFR Fund, plus two off-list firms with calls on my calendar: HOMA and Brightwater Games Fund)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels (Makers Fund, Raine, BBQ Capital, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, General Catalyst, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo Capital, e2vc, Treo VC)
- Keep warm: 2 firms, 0 angels (LVP, Hiro Capital)
Total: 24 firms and 1 angel.

Build access for the firms in talks: Dentsu and T-Accelerate are iOS only. Everyone else in talks has none. Arthur's Play tester list was still not attached to the internal test track as of Sep 30, so the Android adds don't work yet.

Staying off (worth knowing for Monday):
- Paul Heydon: pulled out Sep 30 and never signed.
- Play Ventures, Lakestar, Grishin and March/1AM Gaming: passed without a call.
- Mattel: since the kickoff it's only been RFP talk.
- Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri Detsaridis, Transcend and Acterra: nothing from us since Sep 3.

On the Existing Investor Update card, I added checklists for New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm (Keep warm didn't exist yet). I also added 19 "F/up with" cards in To Do. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) have meetings on my calendar, so they don't get cards. For NCsoft I commented on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of adding another.

See you Monday.

Fred

content.text:
Everything is ready for Monday's review: the send list is in your folder, the Trello work is done, and I've replied on Leonard's thread with the counts. The groups follow his rules doc and reflect where things stood at end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific).

**Who's in each group (24 firms, 1 angel)**
- **New investor – 1 angel:** Anton Bernstein, $25,000. He cut from $40K to $25K, and DocuSign shows the $25K SAFE as Completed on Sep 26, which is Leonard's test for "signed."
- **In talks – 8 firms:** a16z, NCsoft, Dentsu Ventures, SciPlay, T-Accelerate, GFR Fund, HOMA and Brightwater Games Fund. HOMA and Brightwater aren't on the 2025 list, but both had calls on your calendar.
- **Awaiting reply – 14 firms:** Makers Fund, Raine, BBQ Capital, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, General Catalyst, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo Capital, e2vc, Treo VC.
- **Keep warm – 2 firms:** LVP and Hiro Capital. Both passed after a call.

**Game build access:** only Dentsu and T-Accelerate can get the test build, and on iOS only. Arthur's Android tester list was never connected to the internal test track as of Sep 30, so Android doesn't work for any investor yet.

**Left off:**
- Paul Heydon pulled out on Sep 30 without signing.
- Play Ventures, Lakestar, Grishin and March/1AM Gaming said no without ever having a call.
- With Mattel it's only been RFP talk since the Sep 3 kickoff.
- Kevin Lin, Mike Fischer, Demetri Detsaridis, Transcend and Acterra haven't heard from us since Sep 3.

**What I did**
- **Sheet:** a Google Sheet named "Q4 update - send list" (the name the README asks for) in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, with edit access for Leonard. Each row has the group, amount, build access and a short note on why it's in that group.
- **Existing Investor Update card:** four checklists, one per group, with one item per firm or angel (25 items). The Keep warm checklist didn't exist yet, so I created it too.
- **To Do list:** 19 "F/up with …" cards for the firms in talks or awaiting reply.
  - Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) already have meetings on your calendar, so they don't get cards.
  - NCsoft already had a "F/up with Anel" card, so I commented on that instead of adding a new one.
- **Email:** replied on Leonard's thread with the counts. It went to Leonard only; Robert and Arthur weren't copied.

**Calls you may want to check on Monday**
- **General Catalyst** is in Awaiting reply because IH contacted them on our behalf. Leonard's own email to them bounced.
- **Treo VC** contacted us first; Leonard sent them the deck on Sep 3. I counted that as our outreach.
- **Initial Capital** said they won't lead but might write a small check. I didn't treat that as a no.
- **a16z** is in talks: the speedrun interview counts as a call, and their speedrun rejection isn't an answer on the bridge.
